as_told.title: Guidance Technologies closes and Northrop's electrogravitics paper

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how an inventor named Townsend Brown, who worked on using electric charge to push or lift craft, ran a company in Santa Monica, California, called Guidance Technologies, and that in the fall of 1967 he shut it down with no explanation, saying he got no results. Michels says that soon after, in 1968, the aircraft maker Northrop, linked to the wealthy investor Floyd Odlum, wrote a paper saying it was investing in this kind of electric propulsion, and he connects it to the Air Force general Curtis LeMay, the jet maker Bill Lear, and an Aviation Week magazine report on the B-2 stealth bomber. The suggestion is that Brown's work quietly went into secret aerospace projects.
